summary: Frail 88-year-old (Clinical Frailty Scale 7, ASA IV, eGFR 28) with ultrasound-confirmed acute calculous cholecystitis: the decision layer ranks gallbladder drainage above early laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

inputs.hpi: Two days of constant right upper quadrant pain after a fatty meal, radiating to the right shoulder tip, with nausea and one vomit. Fever overnight. Lives in a care home, mobilises with a frame, dependent for personal care. Hypertension, chronic kidney disease, heart failure.

exam.abdomen: Tender right upper quadrant with a positive Murphy's sign; no generalised peritonism; no palpable mass.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Gallstones with a thickened 6 mm gallbladder wall, pericholecystic fluid and a sonographic Murphy's sign. CBD 5 mm.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute calculous cholecystitis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute calculous cholecystitis, TG18 grade II, in a frail 88-year-old (CFS 7, ASA IV).

mustInclude.note: TG18: poor performance status / high CCI or ASA → drainage; frailty raises operative harm.

match: re:observe rather than early laparoscopic cholecystectomy
mustInclude.note: Early LC is not advised for this patient at the point estimate.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — flowchart for the management of acute cholecystitis
guideline.citation: Okamoto K et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci 2018;25:55-72.

guideline.name: CHOCOLATE randomised trial
guideline.section: LC vs percutaneous drainage in high-risk patients

guideline.name: CPOC/BGS perioperative care for people living with frailty

rationale: TG18 recommends early cholecystectomy only for patients fit for surgery (CCI and ASA); for the frail and those with severe comorbidity, gallbladder drainage and antibiotics. CHOCOLATE favoured LC in moderately high-risk patients (APACHE-II 7-14), not in the frail with severe comorbidity.
